statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays in the low band because the overnight futures drift is contained and crude has paused its rally, removing Thursday's principal amplifier, while Stress remains elevated on a 30-year Treasury yield at its highest since 2004.
recommendation: December NQ futures print 30,692.50, about 0.24% below the 30,766.75 settle, inside a 30,681.75-30,765.25 evening band on roughly 10,500 contracts. The drift lower since the Globex reopen is gradual and low-volume rather than an efficient one-way extension, and it follows a cash session in which the Nasdaq-100 retraced a 0.87% decline in full to close at 30,478.86, up 0.03%. Completed two-way retracement plus a contained evening range is the opposite of the persistent mean-reversion failure the Tail score measures, so Tail is held at 18 in the low band. Stress stays at 55 because the macro backdrop remains difficult: the 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.444% on Thursday, its highest since 2004, the 10-year traded near 5.1% at levels last seen in 2007, mortgage rates rose to 7.37%, and roughly 69% odds of an October rate increase are discounted. The one clear improvement is crude, with WTI near $93.85 and Brent near $105.93 after declines of 0.80% and 0.63% that pause a Thursday advance to settles of $94.61 and $106.60. Index internals remain dispersed rather than aligned, with Meta up 4.5% and Alphabet up 1.34% against Arm down 7.88% and Broadcom down 1.3%, which undercuts the coordinated impulse a genuine Tail path usually requires. Confidence is 86 on fresh verified futures, index, volatility, crude, yield and calendar evidence; the shared Finviz context was about 55 minutes old but partial, missing its futures and calendar sections, so cross-asset confirmation came from independent primary sources.
headline: December NQ futures drift to 30,692.50, down 0.24%, in a contained overnight band; Tail holds at 18 as crude pauses its rally
body: The Nasdaq-100 enters Friday's overnight session without the one-way structure that would change the Tail reading. Thursday's cash session traded down to 30,204.16, roughly 0.87% below the 30,470.29 previous close, then recovered the entire decline to a 30,529.35 high and settled at 30,478.86, up 8.56 points. Since the Globex reopen, December NQ futures have worked gradually lower to 30,692.50 within a 30,681.75-30,765.25 band on roughly 10,500 contracts, a drift of about 0.24% from settlement spread across several hours of thin trade. The dominant background remains the global long-end bond rout: the 30-year Treasury yield climbed above 5.44% on Thursday, its highest since 2004, and the 10-year reached about 5.1%, a level last seen in 2007, as resilient growth data, higher energy prices and renewed inflation concern pulled additional Federal Reserve tightening into the curve. Traders discount roughly 69% odds of a further rate increase by the end of October, and mortgage rates have risen to 7.37%, the highest since May 2024. Against that, crude has paused: WTI trades near $93.85 and Brent near $105.93 after declines of 0.80% and 0.63% from Thursday settles of $94.61 and $106.60, as reports continue that US and Iranian negotiators are working toward a phased agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Volatility remains contained, with the VIX at 15.67 after fading from a 16.57 session high. Dispersed index internals complete the picture. The named conditions that would change the Tail reading are a renewed crude leg above Thursday's highs, a disorderly extension of the long-end move during European hours, or observed shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after Friday's 13:30Z cash open.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the Claude Tail estimate ranged from 17 to 25 and spent most of the period in the watch band. The single orange print came at 09:00Z during the European morning, when a trend-down read pushed Tail to 25. From the US cash open onward the estimate drifted back down as the index recovered its intraday decline, and the window closed with five consecutive low-band readings of 19, 19, 19, 18 and 18. Stress stayed elevated throughout, between 49 and 58, reflecting the continuing long-end yield rout rather than any observed breakdown in mean reversion.
outlookSummary: The overnight path runs through Asian and European hours with no scheduled US release until Friday's 12:30Z data block, so the conditional estimate stays in the low-to-watch band and rises mainly at liquidity transitions: the Tokyo close at 06:00Z and the European cash and bond open at 07:00Z, where a disorderly continuation of the long-end move is the most credible conditional route to persistent equity pressure. The concentrated window is 12:25Z to 14:15Z, covering August Durable Goods Orders at 12:30Z, the Fed Schmid speech at 13:20Z, the 13:30Z cash open and final Michigan sentiment with its five-year inflation expectation at 14:00Z. Fed Hammack speaks at 18:00Z into thinning Friday liquidity, and approaching quarter-end can distort the final cash hour. CME equity index futures close for the weekend at 21:00Z, after which path-dependent risk falls and Confidence steps down because no live price evidence is produced.
